checks: Read s350 (code) and s350/s351 outputs and the 3 report entries; numbers in report.json match out/q59/s350.txt and s351.txt (H13CN/HCN N 0.0221+-0.0075, S 0.0014+-0.0098; H13CO+/HCO+ N 0.0284+-0.0058, S 0.0128+-0.0064). I did not re-run the cube fits; I audited the method instead.

Method is sound: one common circular beam, same aperture and window for 12C and 13C, joint fit of neighbouring lines (SiO, HN13C, CCH) with local baseline, error = line-free rms x null-aperture calibration (floor = null std), 384 variants, +5% cross-EB scale. Agree. Noise/null test is done and the variant spread is added to the statistical error. Nominal N H13CO+/HCO+ (0.038 at the peak pixel, 2.2 arcsec) is consistent with Harada+18 Table 13 (0.046+-0.005 at 1.7 arcsec). Agree.

Significance calibration: N H13CN ~4.3 sigma stat (~3 sigma with spread), N H13CO+ ~7 sigma stat, S H13CO+ ~2-3 sigma, S H13CN not detected. The worker labels them correctly (suggestive, not decisive, S H13CN consistent with 0). Agree with the verdict that 2015.1.00993 cannot decide the p0059 question, and that p0059's 'N/S 3+-3.5' is reproduced.

Physical reading: D>1 for BOTH species at similar level (H13CO+ direct N/S 2.2, 1.7 sigma from 1) points to a nuclear-wide 13C/12C difference (opacity and/or 12C/13C), not an HCN-specific one; at N the 13C HCN/HCO+ (0.78) equals the 12C ratio (0.83), so no evidence HCN is more opaque than HCO+. This is a useful, honestly stated exclusion. Opacity tau(HCO+) N ~1.3, HCN ~0.65 with a 12C/13C prior of 40-100; degenerate with X as stated. Agree.

Caveats I would insist on in the post: (i) the 'mean over 384 variants' mixes pixel, 0.5 theta and theta apertures, which for the compact N core change the ratio by ~40% (0.027 to 0.038); quote a standard configuration plus the range, and say the 13C/12C ratio at N depends on beam dilution of a compact core. (ii) The D posterior for H13CN (median 5.8, P(D>2)=0.86, BF 6.7) and the C13 contrast posterior (P>1.45 = 0.8) are driven by the log-flat prior and a single N detection with S consistent with zero; the only prior-robust statements are D_95%-lower ~1.2 and the H13CO+ direct ratio 2.2+-1.2. Present those, not the medians. (iii) H13CO+ and HCO+ come from different spws/EBs, so the 5% scale is assumed, not measured.
notes_for_questioner: Decisive S H13CN/HCN needs sigma ~0.003 (~10x deeper than 2015.1.00993); check whether any other archive project covers H13CN/H13CO+ 1-0 or 3-2 (e.g. H13CN 3-2 / H13CO+ 3-2 in Band 7, or the 2017.1.00379 data's own 12C/13C-sensitive lines such as HC15N, H13CN 3-2 at 259.0 GHz in the Band 6 setup) at N and S, which would give the same test with the existing 0.2-1 arcsec data. Then feed the 13C ratios and the opacity posteriors into a joint non-LTE (RADEX) fit of N and S with 12C 1-0/3-2 ladders (Q57), keeping 12C/13C N vs S as a free nuisance parameter. Also ask: does a nuclear-wide 13C/12C difference (D>1 for both species) match the N 12C/13C of 31-50 preferred in Q40, and what does that imply for HCN/HCO+ 12C contrast being abundance-driven?
